title: Flexible outcome models reduced but did not remove transport bias where the target left the data, and could not see a modification they were not built to see
question: Do flexible outcome models remove the transport bias a parametric STC incurs under threshold, hinge and covariate-interaction surfaces, and with valid intervals, as overlap worsens?
design: Binary-outcome source trial with one adversarial surface feature at a time and targets at three distances; parametric STC, a GAM with smooth modification and a structured GAM with linear modification, standardized by G-computation. 12 cells, 500 replicates each.
answer: Largely yes, the refuting sentence holds. Under a hinge in the treatment effect at a target 1.5 SD from the source, parametric STC was biased by -0.144 and a GAM with smooth treatment modification by -0.085 (coverage 0.93): about 40% less bias, short of the registered halving, with the same RMSE (0.314 against 0.318) because its variance was larger. Under a covariate-by-covariate modification every method was biased by about -0.18, since additive smooths cannot represent a product. A threshold prognostic term largely cancelled in all methods.
findings: Bias grew with target distance for every method on the hinge and product surfaces.
The structured GAM (smooth prognosis, linear modification) was no better than STC on the hinge surface.
Coverage stayed near 0.90 to 0.93 in biased cells because intervals were wide (empirical SD about 0.3).
not_answered: No BART, random forest, doubly robust or ML-NMR arm; logit link, one sample size; model-based intervals only. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Target-population marginal log odds ratio, A versus C
